title: Release a service to production
summary: Take a tested change from staging to production with an approved change record, a watched roll-out and a rollback if something goes wrong. Use it for every release of a tier 0, 1 or 2 service.

resources.title: Release checklist template
resources.description: Copy into the change record: what changes, who watches, how to roll back.

resources.title: Skill: prepare a release
resources.description: Writes the release notes from the merged pull requests and fills in the change record.

resources.title: Change freeze calendar
resources.description: Dates when no production release is allowed.

prerequisites.title: A build pipeline that produces signed images
prerequisites.description: Only images built and signed by the pipeline can be deployed to production.

prerequisites.title: Monitoring and alerts for the service
prerequisites.description: You need a dashboard to watch the roll-out and alerts that page the on-call engineer.

prerequisites.title: The change is deployed and tested in staging
prerequisites.description: The same image version you will release has passed the automated tests in staging.

actors.name: You
actors.description: The engineer who releases the change.

actors.name: Site Reliability team
actors.description: Slack #sre. Watches tier 0 releases with you.

steps.title: Check there is no change freeze
instructions: Open the change freeze calendar.
Check that your release date is not inside a freeze period.
Check that no other release of a service you depend on is planned for the same hour.

steps.title: Write the release notes
instructions: List the merged pull requests since the last release.
Describe in one sentence each what changes for users.
Name the database changes and feature flags, if any.
Write how to roll back: the previous image version and any manual step.
steps.outcome: Release notes with a rollback plan

steps.title: Raise the change record
instructions: Catalogue item: Standard change - service release.
Paste the release notes and the rollback plan.
Enter the service id, the image version and the planned start and end time.
Name who watches the release with you.

steps.title: Fix the change record
instructions: Read the change manager's comment.
Add what is missing, usually the rollback plan or the test evidence.
Submit the change for approval again.

steps.title: Is it a tier 0 service?
instructions: Look up the tier of the service in the service catalogue.

steps.title: Book an SRE to watch the release
steps.description: For tier 0 services an SRE joins the release call and watches the error rate with you.

steps.title: Start the production deployment
instructions: Open the release workflow of your repository.
Run 'Deploy to production' with the image version from the change record.
Put the change number in the run description.

steps.title: Roll out to 10%, then to all
steps.description: Argo CD sends 10% of the traffic to the new version for 15 minutes, then the rest when the error rate stays normal.

steps.title: Watch the dashboard during the roll-out
instructions: Open the service dashboard in Grafana.
Compare error rate and response time with the hour before the release.
Run the smoke tests against production.

steps.title: Release healthy?
instructions: Answer No when the error rate or the response time is clearly higher than before the release, or a smoke test failed.

steps.title: Roll back to the previous version
steps.description: Roll back first and investigate afterwards. If customers were affected, raise an incident.
instructions: Run 'Deploy to production' with the previous image version.
Check the error rate returns to normal.
If customers noticed the problem, start the incident process.
Set the change record to 'Backed out' with what you saw.

steps.title: Close the change record
instructions: Set the change record to 'Implemented successfully'.
Post the release notes in the team channel.
